sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4,319 million in FY2016 to $34,639 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].

The path was a step change, not a straight line: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% in FY2024 and 34.3% in FY2025 [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump came from a 64% increase in Data Center revenue and the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product sales [P46].
The FY2023 decline was a 25% drop in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [P35].
FY2025 growth was driven by Data Center and Client and Gaming, partly offset by a 3% decline in Embedded [P15].
Data Center revenue reached $16,635 million in FY2025, 48.0% of total revenue, and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% growth [S98][D692][D694][D483].
Data Center revenue rose 32% on strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPU accelerators [P13].
Client and Gaming revenue of $14,550 million contributed 19.0pp, with Client up 51% on a 31% increase in processor unit shipments and a 15% rise in average selling price [S101][D701][P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% against 164.2% net income growth, as the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Operating margin of 10.7% in FY2025 sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high, up 0.2pp, as product mix gains were partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and related charges [F40][D498][P14].
The FY2025 operating margin rose 3.3pp, with cost of revenue adding 0.2pp, R&D 1.7pp and SG&A subtracting 1.2pp [D499][D513][D514][D515].
SG&A rose 48.9% in FY2025, and selling and marketing expense reached $2,400 million, 6.9% of revenue [D503][X60][D463].

Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin because a $103 million tax benefit and $577 million of other income, mainly unrealized investment gains, lifted net income [F80][F60][X113][X123][P4][P5].
Operating cash flow of $7,709 million was 1.78x net income and free cash flow of $6,735 million was 1.55x, against a window median of 1.17x [F110][F70][D470][F130][D471][D810].
Free cash flow margin reached 19.4%, near the 19.6% window high, versus a 6.5% median [D467][D803][D804].
Operating cash flow was lifted by $4.3 billion of net income and $4.6 billion of non-cash adjustments, partly offset by a $2.2 billion inventory build for Data Center products [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Cash and investments of $10,552 million against total debt of $4,096 million left net cash of $6,456 million, 18.6% of revenue [D474][D475][D476][D477].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of six semis peers, whose median is -13.9% of revenue [D826][D827].
Debt rose 138.0% on $1.5 billion of new notes issued in March 2025, which also lifted interest expense to $131 million [D508][P6][X93].
Buybacks of $1,316 million absorbed 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
Total debt rose 138.0% in FY2025 to $4,096 million, but net cash still rose to $6,456 million, so leverage is not a concern [D508][D475][D476].

Operating margin of 10.7% ranks only at the 17th percentile of six semis peers against a 31.0% median, and return on equity of 7.2% is at the 17th percentile versus 26.7% [F60][D818][D819][D482][D830][D831].
The FY2025 effective tax rate fell 21.3pp to -2.5%, mainly from an $853 million benefit on released uncertain tax positions, so net margin is flattered [D469][D412][P4].
Days inventory outstanding rose to 165 days from 160, extending a build from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
If operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median in the FY2026 10-K, the FY2025 recovery is durable; a slip toward the 1.8% FY2023 level would reverse it [D795][F58].
Watch free cash flow margin against the 19.6% window high; a drop below the 6.5% median would signal the inventory build is consuming cash [D803][D804].
Watch Data Center revenue growth against the 32.2% FY2025 rate; a deceleration would remove the largest contributor to growth [D693].
